speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This Bill contains a number of amendments to several Acts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Most of the amendments are minor and technical in nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: First, clause 2 of the Bill amends section 55(7)(b) of the Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act (BMSMA) to correct a typographical error.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The existing section 55(7)(b) of BMSMA provides that an individual cannot be appointed as a treasurer if he is already the chairperson or secretary; and the re-appointment would result in the individual holding office as a treasurer for three consecutive terms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The two limbs of section 55(7)(b) should be disjunctive, and not conjunctive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 2 of the Bill corrects this typographical error, by substituting the word "and " between the two limbs with the word "or ".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Next, let me touch on the amendment to the Control of Plants Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The existing definition of "prohibited pesticide" in section 2 of the Act refers to the Tenth Schedule to the Food Regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: However, the Food Regulations have since been revised, and the previous Tenth Schedule is now the Ninth Schedule.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 3 of the Bill introduces an amendment to the Control of Plants Act to update the existing reference from the Tenth Schedule to the Ninth Schedule.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Third, let me come to the amendments to the National Arts Council Act and the Singapore Sports Council Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Instead, the Minister will have the flexibility to appoint a Deputy Chairman in appropriate situations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This flexibility will allow the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) to better address the needs of these two Statutory Boards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: A savings provision has been included to preserve the appointment of existing members and officeholders of the NAC and the SSC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Singapore Sports Council Act will also be amended to provide that the Chief Executive Officer of the SSC may be appointed as a member of the Council, in an ex officio capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Next, let me turn to the amendments to the Penal Code.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 5(1) of the Bill rectifies a potential technical drafting gap that could arise once section 8 of the Criminal Law Reform Act (CLRA) 2019 comes into force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The amendment is for the sole purpose of removing this potential technical drafting gap, which I will explain to Members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The existing section 40(2) of the Penal Code allows for the right of private defence to be raised as a defence to non-Penal Code offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This right of private defence is currently set out in Chapter IV of the Penal Code.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: CLRA moves the provisions relating to the right of private defence to the new Chapter IVA of the Penal Code.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Before this move can take effect, a new reference to "Chapter IVA " must be inserted into the existing section 40(2) of the Penal Code as a consequential amendment, to clarify that the provisions relating to the right of private defence will continue to apply for non-Penal Code offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This amendment is intended to preserve the status quo under the current Penal Code, so that the right to private defence can be raised as a defence for non-Penal Code offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: I will also be proposing an amendment to the Bill during the Committee stage, to amend section 26D of the Penal Code, which has not yet been brought into force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This amendment will ensure that when section 26D of the Penal Code is brought into force, there will be no change or deviation from the current law on wilful blindness, which was the intention when this House passed the CLRA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Section 26D of the Penal Code was introduced under CLRA to codify the common law definition of knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Its current form reflects the Penal Code Review Committee’s decision not to provide for the concept of "wilful blindness" as part of section 26D.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Committee had assessed the case law, and especially the Court of Appeal’s decision in 2011 in Nagaenthran a/l K Dharmalingam v Public Prosecutor   4 SLR 1156, and concluded that "wilful blindness" was simply an evidential tool used to infer that an accused had knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Committee concluded that there was thus no need to provide for the concept of "wilful blindness" in section 26D.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: After the passage of CLRA, however, the Court of Appeal delivered its decision in Adili Chibuike Ejike v Public Prosecutor   2 SLR 254.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Court of Appeal held that "wilful blindness" is properly described as a mental state falling short of knowledge but which is legally deemed to be equivalent to knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Court described this as an "extended conception of wilful blindness", where "it can almost be said" that the accused persons knew the fact in question.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Therefore, if section 26D is brought into force as it was originally drafted, this would abolish the "extended conception of wilful blindness" under this case authority.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The amendment does not in any way prejudice accused persons, as it does not expand the common law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Court of Appeal limited this "extended conception of wilful blindness" to the context of knowledge for the purpose of proving possession under section 18(1) of the Misuse of Drugs Act in this case and recognised that it may be different with respect to knowledge of the nature of the drug under section 18(2) of the Misuse of Drugs Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: However, Members would note that the proposed amendment to section 26D does not set out all these three elements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This is to allow for further development of the doctrine of "wilful blindness" by the common law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This is important because the Court of Appeal had suggested that the doctrine might apply slightly differently in practice, depending on what specific fact an accused is said to have been wilfully blind towards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Next, let me turn to the Singapore Corporation of Rehabilitative Enterprises Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: SCORE’s new name will be announced once the rebranding exercise is complete.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As the amendments are related, may I seek your permission to move them together?
